sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface display confirmed by indirect immunofluorescence flow cytometry on intact non-permeabilized P. pastoris cells (L2); enzymatic activity of the FLAG-tagged surface-displayed AChE was NOT MEASURED in the cited clips.
sites.rationale: Human ACHE has a signal peptide spanning residues 1–31 (authoritative landmark); the mature N-terminus begins at residue 32 (E). A tag placed after residue 31 is therefore on the extracellular face, well clear of any TM boundary (the protein is GPI-anchored with no TM helix). Python verification confirms residue 31 = A and residue 32 = E in the canonical sequence. No specific residue number is cited in L1 or L3/L4; the position is topology-derived from the single free extracellular terminus of the mature protein. L1 (BmAChE) and L3/L4 (DmAChE) are both indirect evidence (insect orthologs), but both independently place a FLAG tag at the N-terminus of the full-length, membrane-anchored AChE, mapping to the same junction in human ACHE. BmAChE (Bombyx mori AChE, ortholog of human ACHE) was expressed as a full-length fusion with an α-agglutinin (AGα1) membrane anchor in P. pastoris, with a FLAG tag placed at the N-terminus of the AChE coding sequence. The construct is membrane-anchored and surface-displayed; the FLAG is on the extracellular face. Surface display was confirmed by indirect immunofluorescence flow cytometry on intact (non-permeabilized) yeast cells (L2). A second independent ortholog construct (DmAChE-FLAG-Agα in S. cerevisiae, L3/L4) corroborates the same N-terminal junction.

sources.claim: The bmace-AGα1 gene with a FLAG tag (eight amino acids) at the N -terminus of AChE was subcloned into the expression vector pPIC9K.

literature_notes: All four ledger clips concern insect AChE orthologs (BmAChE from Bombyx mori, L1/L2; DmAChE from Drosophila melanogaster, L3/L4) expressed as surface-display fusions with α-agglutinin anchors in yeast. No clip reports a tag insertion in full-length human ACHE itself. Both ortholog papers place a FLAG tag at the N-terminus of the mature AChE (after signal peptide cleavage), which maps to insert_after_residue = 31 in human ACHE canonical numbering. Because both papers support the same junction, this is reported as one site (L1 as primary clip, L3/L4 corroborating). Human ACHE is GPI-anchored; the C-terminus carries the GPI signal peptide that is cleaved during GPI attachment, making a C-terminal tag incompatible with native membrane anchoring — no ledger clip supports a C-terminal site. No internal loop insertions are supported by any ledger clip.
